instructions: Bring a medium pot of water to a boil over high heat.
Add the rice cakes and cook them for 1 to 2 minutes, until they're soft and bend without cracking. Fresh, soft rice cakes only need about 30 seconds.
Drain them and pat them dry with paper towels. Wet rice cakes spatter in the oil.
Thread 3 or 4 rice cakes onto each skewer, side by side through their middles, leaving a handle at one end. That should be about 8 skewers.
Mince the garlic. In a small saucepan off the heat, stir together the 2 tbsp gochujang, 3 tbsp ketchup, the garlic, 1 tbsp jam, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1/8 tsp black pepper and 1 tbsp water.
Set the saucepan over medium heat and stir for about 1 minute, until the sauce bubbles and turns glossy and a little thicker. Take it off the heat.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Add half the skewers in one layer.
Cook them for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is crisp and puffed in spots. Flip them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes.
Transfer them to a plate. Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and cook the rest the same way.
Brush or spoon the sauce over both sides of every skewer.
Sprinkle the 1 tsp sesame seeds over the top and serve warm.
method_notes: Every version softens the rice cakes, threads them onto skewers, crisps them in a little oil and brushes on a sweet gochujang sauce. Beyond Kimchee (the lead) uses gochujang, ketchup, garlic, strawberry jam and honey; Food Network adds cocktail franks and corn syrup and Sift & Simmer adds soy sauce and rice vinegar. This follows Beyond Kimchee with brown sugar from Sift & Simmer in place of the honey to keep it vegan, a little less gochujang and a little more ketchup so it stays mild, and sesame seeds in place of the chopped nuts to keep it nut-free. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no version of this dish, so this leads with the best version read.
